headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates large energy users, such as data centers, to bear the costs of their required grid infrastructure upgrades, preventing these expenses from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor's administration, state lawmakers.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia orders data centers to pay for new transmission infrastructure.
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission has ordered data centers to cover the costs of transmission infrastructure built exclusively for their facilities. This decision, supported by the Governor's administration, aims to prevent these expenses from being spread across other utility customers, potentially saving Virginia families and businesses hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and aiding in water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local communities, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Potomac Conservancy.
news_headline: SB553: Data Centers Water Use Reporting Becomes Law.
news_summary: SB553, now law, mandates water suppliers to report water usage by data centers to the State Water Control Board. This legislation provides the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality with crucial data for informed decisions on water resources, addressing concerns about dwindling groundwater supplies due to high data center consumption.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to evaluate noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to consider other environmental effects.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Virginia Requires Data Center Site Assessments for Noise.
news_summary: HB153 mandates that Virginia localities require site assessments for new data centers over 100 megawatts, specifically examining noise impacts on residential units and schools within 500 feet. The bill also allows localities to assess effects on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forests, empowering local governments with more information for development decisions.
